title: Naval Topic 2 生词 · 英英解释

items.ex: Conventional wisdom is what most people believe is true, often without checking. Naval uses it for the common idea that happy people stop trying. We often say it right before we question it.
exs: Conventional wisdom says you need a degree to do well, but plenty of people prove it wrong.
The conventional wisdom is that mornings are best for workouts.

items.ex: Practical means it comes from real life and real doing, not from theory. Practical earned experience is what you learned the hard way, by living it. It's also used for things that are useful and sensible.
exs: Wearing flat shoes at work is just more practical.
She gave me some practical tips for my first week.

items.ex: To replicate means to make a copy of something, or, for living things, to reproduce. Naval means humans are built to survive and have kids. In everyday talk, we use it for copying a result or a style.
exs: I tried to replicate the lash style from her photo.
It's hard to replicate that kind of success twice.

items.zh: 有干劲的；有强烈进取心的
items.ex: Driven describes someone with a strong inner push to reach goals. It's stronger than just hardworking. Americans often use it as a compliment.
exs: She's really driven; she opened her own salon at twenty-five.
You don't have to be driven every single day.

items.ex: Motivated means you have a reason and the energy to do something. You can feel motivated today and not tomorrow, so it's more about a state than a personality. We say get motivated or stay motivated.
exs: I'm more motivated when I have a clear plan.
How do you stay motivated when you're tired?

items.zh: 竞技场；（比喻）真正行动、竞争的场合
items.ex: An arena is a big place for sports or shows. Naval uses it as a picture: living in the arena means being out there, acting and taking risks, not just watching. It's a famous image from a Theodore Roosevelt speech.
exs: She stepped into the political arena last year.
Stop watching from the side and get into the arena.

items.ex: If something is aligned with your values or goals, it fits them and points the same way. Naval wants work that matches what he believes needs to be done. It's common in work and self-help talk.
exs: This job is finally aligned with what I care about.
Make sure your daily habits are aligned with your goals.

items.ex: Uniquely means in a way that only you, or only this thing, can. What I can uniquely do means the things nobody else can do quite like me. It points to your special strengths.
exs: She's uniquely good at calming nervous clients.
This city is uniquely beautiful in the fall.

items.zh: 从这个意义上说；这样看来
items.ex: In that sense means from that point of view, or thinking about it that way. Speakers use it to sum up what they just explained. It's a smooth way to connect ideas.
exs: The job pays less, but I'm happier, so in that sense it's better.
In that sense, every mistake is a lesson.

items.ex: Likely means probably. Here it works like an adverb: your definition will likely change. Very common in American English, both spoken and written.
exs: It'll likely rain this afternoon, so bring an umbrella.
She's likely to be a little late.

items.ex: A realization is the moment you suddenly understand something clearly. Chris asks if Naval could have understood this without success first. We often say come to the realization that.
exs: I came to the realization that I needed more rest.
It was a big realization for me.

items.ex: An ascetic is a person who gives up comfort and pleasure, often for spiritual reasons. Naval says he didn't want to live with nothing, like a monk. Pronounced uh-SET-ik.
exs: He lived like an ascetic, with almost no furniture.
I'm not going to live an ascetic life just to save money.

items.ex: To renounce means to formally or completely give something up. Renounce everything means give up all possessions and desires. It sounds serious and is less casual than give up.
exs: She renounced her old habits and started fresh.
He renounced his citizenship.

items.ex: Unrealistic means not possible or not reasonable in real life. Naval felt giving up everything was not realistic for him. We use it a lot for goals and expectations.
exs: Losing ten pounds in a week is unrealistic.
Don't set unrealistic goals for yourself.

items.ex: The Buddha was a prince who left his palace to search for the meaning of life. Naval tells his story as the opposite path: giving up wealth first. Americans say BOO-duh.
exs: There's a small Buddha statue in her studio.
The story of the Buddha is about letting go.

items.ex: A route is a way to get somewhere, and here, a way to reach a goal in life. The happy route means the path that keeps him happy. Americans say both ROOT and ROWT.
exs: I take the same route to work every day.
There's more than one route to success.

items.ex: To involve means to include something as a necessary part. A route that involves material success includes making money along the way. Very common in everyday English.
exs: My job involves a lot of talking with clients.
What does the training involve?
